deities: Bhadrakali (Thirumandhamkunnilamma, north-facing, with the Saptamatrikas in the Mathrusala)
Shiva (sacred split linga in the roofless Sreemoolasthanam)
festivals: Thirumandhamkunnu Pooram — 11 days from the Makayiram star in Meenam (March–April), with daily Aarattu and caparisoned elephants
Mangalya Pooja — special wedding oblation attracting thousands of young women
Annual Mandhatha pooja on Chithra in Midhunam

history.dynasty: Valluvanad Rajas (the deity was their paradevatha); Zamorin patronage in later centuries
history.period: Ancient; Pooram attested to the early decades of the 16th century in palm-leaf records
history.summary: One of the three great Bhagavathi temples of Kerala (with Kodungallur and Panayannarkavu), atop the hill at Angadipuram — the old capital of the Valluvanad Rajavamsham. Legend: King Mandhatha of the Surya dynasty received a Shiva linga from Shiva himself; when Goddess Parvati sought to retrieve it, she chose to remain here as Bhadrakali. The Chaver (martyr-warriors) of the Valluvanad king set out from this temple to the Mamankam at Thirunavaya; their memorial 'chaver thara' stands before the entrance. The thanthri is still from the Kattillamuttam/Panthalakode Brahmin families; the Sreemoolasthanam is roofless, evidence of its kavu origin. IMPORTANT CSV ERROR: the row name 'Kodikuthimala Thirumandhamkunnu Temple' conflates two different places. Kodikuthimala is a 540-m hill station and eco-tourism trekking spot near Perinthalmanna (Amminikkad) with no famous temple — it is NOT where this temple stands. The real Thirumandhamkunnu Temple is at Angadipuram, Malappuram district, which is recorded as the town.

name: Thirumandhamkunnu Temple
town_description: Angadipuram, near Perinthalmanna, was the capital of the medieval Valluvanad kingdom; the Bhagavathy temple crowns its hillock and the town hosts the temple's Pooram grounds.

travel.road: On the hilltop at Angadipuram, off the Perinthalmanna–Valanchery road
